en: Wearing an N95 mask protects your lungs from harmful volcanic ash during an eruption at Taal Volcano.
Avoid wading in floodwaters after a typhoon because they often contain leptospirosis bacteria from rat urine.
If you feel a strong earthquake near the coast, immediately evacuate to higher ground to avoid a tsunami.
If you encounter a Philippine cobra in your yard, slowly back away instead of trying to catch it.
Empty stagnant water in old tires around your house to prevent Aedes mosquitoes from breeding and spreading dengue.
Never play in river channels near Mount Pinatubo because heavy rain can trigger deadly, fast-moving volcanic lahars.
Always swim between the red and yellow flags at La Union beaches to avoid dangerous rip currents.
Drink plenty of water and wear a wide hat during the dry season in Cebu to prevent heatstroke.
During heavy monsoon rains, stay away from steep mountain slopes in Benguet to avoid deadly landslides.
Boil water from shallow wells in flood-prone areas of Pampanga to kill harmful bacteria and prevent cholera.
Watch your step and wear a helmet when exploring the slippery limestone floors of Puerto Princesa Subterranean River.
Wear thick water shoes when walking on coral reefs in Batangas to prevent painful cuts from sharp sea urchins.
